materials.title: Calling the swimming pool
materials.text:
Man: Green Lane Pool. Can I help?
Amy: Hello. Is the pool open on Sunday morning?
Man: Yes, from eight o'clock. Swimming lessons begin at nine, so free swimming stops then.
Amy: Can my little brother come? He's six.
Man: Yes, but an adult must be in the water with him. Children under eight cannot swim here alone.
Amy: Dad will come with us. Do we need swimming hats?
Man: Yes. If you do not have one, you can buy one at the desk.
Amy: Can we bring a ball?
Man: Not during free swimming. There is a ball session on Sunday afternoon.
Amy: Is there somewhere to eat afterwards?
Man: Our café opens at ten. You can take food to the picnic tables outside before that.
Amy: Thank you. We'll bring our hats and a picnic.

questions.prompt: When does free swimming stop on Sunday morning?
questions.explanation: Lessons begin at nine and free swimming stops then. Eight is opening; ten is café opening.

questions.prompt: What must Amy’s six-year-old brother do?
options: Wait until he is ten to visit
Have an adult in the water with him
questions.explanation: Under-eight children require an adult in the water. They need not wait until ten and cannot swim alone.

questions.prompt: Where can visitors buy a swimming hat?
questions.explanation: The man gives the desk as the purchase point; neither tables nor water is a shop.

questions.prompt: May Amy use a ball during free swimming?
options: Only if the ball is small
questions.explanation: Balls are prohibited during free swimming. The exception is a separate afternoon session, not early time or small size.

questions.prompt: What does Amy plan to bring?
options: A new desk and a chair
questions.explanation: She explicitly plans hats and a picnic. Furniture is not requested and a ball cannot be used in free swimming.

materials.title: A call about a tortoise
materials.text:
Aunt: Hello, Ben. Can you look after my tortoise on Saturday?
Ben: Yes. What do I need to do?
Aunt: I'll leave his food in a green box. Give him the amount in the small cup, not the large one.
Ben: Shall I put him in the garden?
Aunt: No. Please leave him in his indoor enclosure. The garden gate is being repaired.
Ben: When should I come?
Aunt: After breakfast, about nine. Check that his water dish is clean and has fresh water.
Ben: Can my friend come and see him?
Aunt: Yes, but just watch. Please don't pick him up.
Ben: What if I have a question?
Aunt: My phone number is on the note beside the enclosure. You can call me.
Ben: Will you be home before dinner?
Aunt: Yes, at five. Thank you for helping.

questions.prompt: Which cup should Ben use for the food?
questions.explanation: The aunt specifies the small cup and rejects the large one. Both would ignore the portion instruction.

questions.prompt: Where should the tortoise stay?
questions.explanation: The garden is unsuitable during gate repair. The enclosure is required; a school bag is never suggested.

questions.prompt: When should Ben arrive?
questions.explanation: After breakfast about nine is the visit time. Five is the aunt’s return; dinner is not his arrival.

questions.prompt: What may Ben’s friend do?
questions.explanation: The friend may watch but must not pick it up. Opening the repaired gate is not permitted.

questions.prompt: How can Ben get help with a question?
options: Call the number on the note
questions.explanation: The note beside the enclosure gives a telephone number. Neither waiting a week nor asking an animal answers the arrangement.

materials.title: Snail’s shopping cart
materials.text:
In a village of talking animals, Snail borrowed Mouse's little cart to bring vegetables home. The cart moved easily on the flat path, and Snail was pleased. He bought a cabbage, three carrots and a bag of potatoes.

On the way back, the path went uphill. The cart became difficult to pull. Rabbit passed and offered to help, but Snail said, "No, thank you. I borrowed it, so I must do everything myself."

Rabbit walked beside him. After a while, Snail stopped to rest. He was tired, and the vegetables were no nearer home.

"Borrowing the cart makes you responsible for returning it," Rabbit said. "It doesn't mean you cannot ask for help."

This time, Snail accepted. Rabbit pulled while Snail pushed from behind. They reached Snail's house and shared a carrot snack. Then Snail cleaned the cart before taking it back.

Mouse asked whether it had been useful. "Very useful," said Snail. "But I needed another pair of paws on the hill." He thanked Mouse for the cart and Rabbit for the help. Next market day, he checked the route and asked Rabbit whether they could shop together.

questions.prompt: Why did Snail borrow the cart?
options: To give Mouse a new house
questions.explanation: The opening states the shopping purpose. Neither racing nor house-building is part of the plan.

questions.prompt: Where did pulling become difficult?
options: On the uphill part of the path
On the flat path at the start
questions.explanation: The climb makes it hard; flat ground was easy and Mouse’s house is not the troublesome route.

questions.prompt: Why did Snail first refuse help?
options: He thought borrowing meant doing all the work alone
questions.explanation: His explanation explicitly links borrowing with doing everything himself. He knows Rabbit, and Mouse owns the cart.

questions.prompt: How did they move the cart together?
options: Snail pulled while Rabbit sat inside
questions.explanation: Their roles are explicitly pull and push. No riding or Mouse carrying occurs.

questions.prompt: What did Snail do before returning the cart?
options: He sold the potatoes to Mouse
questions.explanation: Cleaning prepares the borrowed cart’s return. Repainting and selling food to Mouse are absent.

materials.title: Owl’s morning concert
materials.text:
In a forest of talking animals, Owl wanted to hear the morning birds sing. He usually slept during the early hours, so he asked Squirrel to wake him before sunrise.

Squirrel tapped on his door. Owl opened one eye and said, "I can hear nothing. You are too early." He went back to sleep. A few minutes later, the birds began, but Owl missed their song.

The next day, Squirrel returned at the same time. Owl was annoyed. "Yesterday there was no singing when you came!"

"You asked to be ready before it began," Squirrel replied. "Getting to the clearing takes time."

Owl thought about that. This time, he followed Squirrel along the path. They sat quietly while the sky grew lighter. At first, they heard only leaves moving. Then one bird called, and another answered. Soon the clearing was full of song.

Owl listened until the sun rose. He thanked Squirrel and went home for a long sleep. He had learned that an early invitation could lead to a better view of the beginning. Waiting quietly was part of the concert, not proof that they had come at the wrong time.

questions.prompt: Why did Owl need Squirrel’s help?
options: He usually slept in the early hours
He could not hear any bird sounds
questions.explanation: His sleep schedule makes waking difficult. He can hear and actively wants the song.

questions.prompt: What did Owl do on the first morning?
questions.explanation: He returns to sleep and misses the song. The walk occurs the next day; he never joins the singing.

questions.prompt: Why did Squirrel arrive before the singing?
options: They needed time to reach the clearing
He wanted Owl to miss it
The birds had left the forest
questions.explanation: Travel time explains the early wake-up. The birds remain and Squirrel helps rather than prevents attendance.

questions.prompt: What did they first hear in the clearing?
questions.explanation: Leaves move before the first bird call. No drum or Owl’s singing is described.

questions.prompt: What did Owl learn?
options: A quiet place can never have a concert
Friends should arrive only after every event has finished
Being ready early can mean waiting before an event starts
questions.explanation: The waiting lets him hear the beginning. Quietness does not preclude later song, and arriving after completion would miss it.

materials.title: Helping at the school fair
materials.text:
The school fair needs student helpers. Choose one job and sign up with Ms Reed by Wednesday. Helpers must attend a short meeting at 15:30 on Thursday. The fair is on Saturday.

Job | Time | Place | Main task
Book Corner | 9:00–11:00 | Library entrance | Put books into subject groups and help visitors find them
Game Desk | 10:00–12:00 | Small hall | Explain two simple board games; instructions supplied
Plant Table | 11:00–13:00 | Courtyard | Give visitors plant-care cards; do not offer advice beyond the cards
Welcome Team | 9:30–11:30 | Main gate | Show visitors the map and direct them to activities

Helpers should wear their school badges. Do not bring money to collect from visitors: all payments are handled by adult staff at a separate desk. If you cannot attend after signing up, tell Ms Reed as soon as possible so a replacement can be found.

The Plant Table will move inside the dining room if it rains. The other jobs will stay in their listed places. A sandwich and drink are provided after each helper's two-hour shift. Students are welcome to visit the fair before or after their work, but they must not leave their job early to join an activity.

questions.prompt: Who should a student contact to sign up?
options: A parent at the payment desk
questions.explanation: Ms Reed handles sign-up by Wednesday. Visitors and an unspecified payment-desk parent do not.

questions.prompt: Which job begins at ten?
questions.explanation: Game Desk starts10:00. Book Corner starts9:00 and Welcome Team9:30.

questions.prompt: What should Plant Table helpers use to answer visitors?
questions.explanation: They give care cards and must not go beyond them. Guessing and game rules do not meet this instruction.

questions.prompt: Where will the Plant Table be if it rains?
questions.explanation: The rain arrangement explicitly moves it to the dining room. The other places belong to other jobs.

questions.prompt: Which statement is correct?
options: Helpers may leave early whenever they want a game
Student helpers must bring money to collect fees
questions.explanation: Adults handle payments. Students do not bring collection money and must finish their shifts before activities.

materials.title: Activity packs at the local museum
materials.text:
Visitors aged ten to fourteen can borrow one activity pack from the museum desk. Packs are free, but an adult must leave a contact number. Return the pack before leaving the museum. Each contains instructions and reusable materials.

Pack | Main area | Time needed | Included materials
Pattern Finder | Pottery room | About 30 minutes | Drawing board, paper and pencils
Sound Trail | Music gallery | About 40 minutes | Headphones and an audio player
Object Detective | History room | About 50 minutes | Clue cards and a magnifying glass
Shape Builder | Learning room | About 35 minutes | Wooden shapes and picture cards

The Sound Trail is not available during live music performances because visitors need to hear the player clearly. A notice at the desk gives performance times. Headphones from the pack must be used; do not connect your own equipment to the player.

Pattern Finder drawings may be taken home, but the board and pencils must be returned. Every other pack should come back with all its materials. If something is missing when you receive a pack, tell the desk before you begin. Visitors may borrow a second pack only after returning the first, so that other families have a chance to use them too.

questions.prompt: Which pack usually takes the longest?
questions.explanation: 50 minutes exceeds40 and30. Shape Builder is35 and would also be shorter.

questions.prompt: Where is Shape Builder used?
questions.explanation: The table pairs Shape Builder with the learning room. The other rooms are for other packs.

questions.prompt: When is Sound Trail unavailable?
questions.explanation: Only live-performance conflicts are stated. No daily afternoon ban or ownership-based restriction is given.

questions.prompt: What may Pattern Finder users keep?
questions.explanation: Drawings may go home; board and pencils are reusable and must be returned.

questions.prompt: What must visitors do before borrowing a second pack?
questions.explanation: One pack at a time ensures access for others. Packs are free and must be returned before leaving, not bought.
